items.title: SAP30BP links aberrant splicing and metabolic reprogramming to drive T cell leukemogenesis.
items.abstract: Aberrant splicing, a hallmark of cancer, emerges as a promising therapeutic target and is driven by dysregulated expression and mutations in splicing machinery components. Despite exhibiting minimal mutations in splicing factors, T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) critically relies on splicing perturbations. However, the mechanistic underpinnings remain largely unexplored. Here, we report that T cell malignancies display the most prevalent splicing alterations and heterogeneity across cancer types, leading to a substantial overproduction of splice variants. SAP30BP, frequently overexpressed in T-ALL, actively contributes to this process and aggravates T cell tumorigenesis. Mechanistically, SAP30BP coordinates with the U2 complex to incur an advantageous splicing variant of DDX39B via the suppression of intron retention. Concomitantly, SAP30BP bridges splicing dysregulation and metabolic rewiring by enhancing glycolysis while attenuating mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in T-ALL. Small molecule-mediated targeting of the splicing and metabolic process effectively suppresses aggressive T cell malignancies and confers susceptibility to chemotherapy agents.

items.title: Knowledge of adult Polish women about polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
items.abstract: Assessment of the level of knowledge of adult Polish women about polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) and analysis of the relationship between awareness of symptoms, diagnosis, complications and prevention of PMOS and selected sociodemographic factors, such as age, marital status, place of residence, education and social activity. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 1502 women living in the Silesian metropolitan area using a proprietary paper questionnaire. The survey included questions regarding awareness of symptoms, risk factors, and preventive measures related to PMOS. Associations between awareness of the condition and sociodemographic variables were analyzed using the chi-square test (χ²), with a significance level of p < 0.05. Most participants were aged 21-35, lived in urban areas, had higher education, and were professionally active. PMOS awareness was high; 1,026 women (68.3%) reported having been diagnosed with the disease. The most common symptoms included menstrual irregularities (97.7%), fertility problems (96.6%), insulin resistance (86.6%), acne (82.5%), and overweight/obesity (81.4%). Statistically significant associations were found between PMOS awareness and age (χ² = 129.89; p < 0.001), marital status, and social activity. Women in Poland demonstrate a high level of general knowledge about PMOS, although they often overestimate its prevalence. The results highlight the need for targeted educational efforts focusing on reliable epidemiological data, diagnosis, and the health consequences of the disease, while considering demographic factors to increase awareness and promote prevention.

Small-molecule targeting of CMTM6 induces dual degradation of PD-L1 and SLC1A5 to enhance cancer immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized oncology; however, emerging therapeutic resistance and the pharmacokinetic limitations of monoclonal antibodies necessitate the development of potent, small-molecule alternatives. CMTM6 (CKLF-like MARVEL transmembrane domain-containing protein 6) has recently been identified as a master posttranslational regulator of PD-L1 stability. Here, we characterize GIC-001 and its derivative, GIC-005, as first-in-class small-molecule inhibitors that directly target CMTM6. GIC-001 binds directly to CMTM6, competitively disrupting its association with PD-L1 and the glutamine transporter SLC1A5 (ASCT2) while crucially preserving its interaction with the essential costimulatory ligand CD58. This targeted dissociation facilitates the polyubiquitination and subsequent lysosomal degradation of both PD-L1 and SLC1A5. Consequently, pharmacological inhibition of the CMTM6 axis blunts PD-L1 expression, restricts glutamine uptake in tumor cells, and restores T cell-mediated cytotoxicity. In syngeneic MC38 and Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) models, GIC-001 significantly suppressed tumor progression and prolonged overall survival. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that this efficacy is driven by a profound remodeling of the tumor microenvironment (TME), characterized by the notable expansion of effector and memory CD8 + T cells alongside the repolarization of suppressive macrophages toward an activated phenotype. Furthermore, GIC-001 exhibited durable antitumor efficacy as a monotherapy and synergized with anti-PD-L1 antibodies, and GIC-005 demonstrated potent in vivo activity. Our findings establish CMTM6-targeted small molecules as a distinct class of dual-action agents that integrate immune and metabolic checkpoint modulation, providing a transformative strategy for cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Drug candidate CT7-1 promotes antitumor immunity by targeting SETMAR to activate cGAS-STING-IFN signaling in breast cancer.
items.abstract: The discovery of previously unidentified anti-breast cancer agents with both high efficacy and favorable safety profiles remains an urgent and critical challenge. Recently, repurposing and modifying the anti-Alzheimer drug memantine have drawn growing interest to enhance its pharmacological properties. Here, we synthesized several memantine analogs, among which a honokiol-memantine hybrid named CT7-1 exhibited broad-spectrum and potent antitumor activity, particularly against breast cancer. Notably, CT7-1 suppressed breast cancer patient-derived organoid proliferation across diverse molecular subtypes while showing a superior toxicity profile in normal breast organoids relative to paclitaxel. In vivo, CT7-1 effectively suppressed tumor growth in immunocompromised and immunocompetent mouse models, with enhanced efficacy observed in the presence of an intact immune system. Integrated multiomics analyses revealed that CT7-1 reshaped the tumor microenvironment by increasing CD8 + T cell infiltration and activation, in addition to promoting major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I)-mediated antigen presentation. Mechanistically, CT7-1 directly bound to and inhibited SETMAR, leading to DNA damage and subsequent cGAS-STING pathway activation. This cascade resulted in the production of pro-inflammatory interferons and chemokines, ultimately up-regulating MHC-I expression. Clinically, high SETMAR expression correlated with poor prognosis, diminished immune cell infiltration, and inferior response to immunotherapy in patients with triple-negative breast cancer. In conclusion, we identify CT7-1 as a first-in-class honokiol-memantine hybrid that exerts potent antitumor effects by targeting SETMAR to activate the DNA damage-cGAS-STING-MHC-I axis, thereby enhancing T cell-mediated tumor immunity. This study provides convincing grounds for developing CT7-1 as a promising immunotherapeutic drug for breast cancer.

items.title: From Data to Discovery: Downstream Interpretation of High-Dimensional Omics Data for Precision Medicine.
items.abstract: With growing technological advances over the last several years, an abundance of high-dimensional multi-omics data has been and continues to be generated across various spatial scales, tissues, and diseases. The volume and complexity of these data hold tremendous potential for biological insight that advances our understanding of cell types and states in both healthy and diseased tissue [1]. Integrating multiple data modalities within and across spatial scales enables us to gain a more comprehensive understanding of biological processes in the genome, epigenome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome. These insights are the foundation for identifying disease and treatment response biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis and for advancing targeted therapeutics, precision oncology, and cancer immunotherapy [2].

items.title: Cerebellar Ataxia with Typical Vimentin-IgG-Associated MRI Pattern but Negative Vimentin Antibodies: A Case of Purkinje Cell Autoimmunity.
items.abstract: Bilateral symmetric corticospinal tracts (CSTs) hyperintensities with subacute cerebellar ataxia were recently attributed to vimentin-immunoglobulin G (IgG)-associated astrocytopathy. We questioned whether this magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) pattern is specific to vimentin autoimmunity. We report a 45-year-old woman presenting with subacute cerebellar ataxia, brainstem involvement, and bilateral CSTs hyperintensities on brain MRI. Serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) were tested using cell-based assays (including vimentin-IgG and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP)-IgG) and in-house tissue-based assay (TBA) on rat and mouse tissues. The patient presented with a characteristic MRI pattern of corticospinal tract (CST) involvement, while serological and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tests yielded persistently negative results for vimentin-IgG and GFAP-IgG. Tissue-based assay (TBA) detected Purkinje cell-binding IgG. CSF examination revealed type Ⅲ oligoclonal bands, alongside markedly elevated glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP, 35,570 pg/mL) and neurofilament light chain (NFL, 26,949 pg/mL).Initial management consisted of high-dose methylprednisolone pulse therapy, followed by adjuvant immunoadsorption and B-cell depletion treatment.Three-month post-treatment follow-up MRI demonstrated substantial resolution of CST lesions. Clinically, the patient achieved amelioration of speech and sensory disturbances, though no meaningful reduction in ataxia was observed. Despite the favorable response in neuroimaging and CSF inflammatory biomarkers, the patient remained refractory to both first- and second-line immunotherapies, with persistent functional neurological disability reflected by a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 4. This case featured a clear dissociation between normalized inflammatory markers and sustained clinical impairment. Bilateral symmetric CST hyperintensities are not unique to vimentin autoimmunity and may arise in Purkinje cell-targeted autoimmunity. This vimentin-IgG astrocytopathy phenocopy highlights antigen localization as a key driver of imaging phenotypes and validates TBA for seronegative differential diagnosis.

items.title: Recent therapeutic strategies for HPV-Associated head and neck cancers.
items.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated head and neck cancers (HNCs), particularly oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas (OPSCC), represent a growing global health burden with rapidly increasing incidence over recent decades. These tumours are biologically and clinically distinct from HPV-negative HNCs, occurring more frequently in younger individuals with limited exposure to traditional risk factors such as tobacco and alcohol. HPV-driven oncogenesis is mediated by viral oncoproteins E6 and E7, which disrupt genomic stability through inactivation of p53 and retinoblastoma pathways, promoting uncontrolled proliferation, genomic instability, and treatment resistance. Current therapeutic strategies for HPV-positive HNCs include surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy remaining the standard of care for locoregionally advanced disease. However, improved treatment responses and overall prognosis in HPV-positive patients have stimulated interest in treatment de-escalation strategies aimed at reducing toxicity without compromising efficacy. Minimally invasive surgical approaches, such as transoral robotic surgery, and reduced-intensity radiotherapy regimens show promising functional outcomes. Immunotherapy represents a major advancement in recurrent and metastatic disease, with immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis demonstrating survival benefits in selected patient populations. Emerging approaches include therapeutic vaccines against HPV oncoproteins, adoptive T cell transfer, targeted therapies, oncolytic virotherapy, and gene therapy aimed at silencing E6/E7 expression or restoring tumor suppressor function. Nanomedicine further offers novel platforms for drug delivery, radiosensitization, and immunomodulation, enhancing treatment specificity and efficacy. Despite significant progress, major challenges persist, including limitations in early diagnosis, treatment resistance, biomarker-driven patient selection, and inadequate public awareness of HPV-associated cancer risk. Integration of advanced diagnostics, such as circulating tumor HPV DNA assays and next-generation sequencing, may improve risk stratification and treatment monitoring. Continued research into combination therapies, targeted approaches, and patient-tailored treatment algorithms remains essential to improve outcomes. In summary, evolving therapeutic strategies for HPV-associated HNCs reflect a shift toward precision oncology, focusing on improved survival, reduced toxicity, and personalized interventions driven by molecular tumor characteristics.

items.title: Persistence of Immunogenicity Following a Single Dose of Live Attenuated Hepatitis A Vaccine: A 20-Year Follow-up Study.
items.abstract: The long-term immunogenicity of a single dose of live-attenuated hepatitis A virus (HAV) vaccine has previously been demonstrated, with substantial seroprotection maintained for up to 15 years after vaccination. The present study further evaluated the persistence of immunogenicity and seroprotection 20 years after vaccination. This single-center follow-up study assessed the immunogenicity of a single dose of H2-strain live-attenuated hepatitis A vaccine (BIOVAC-A) in participants who received the vaccine in 2004. Any participant who had received any additional dose of hepatitis A vaccine was excluded. At 20-year follow-up, total anti-HAV antibodies were estimated using enzyme-linked fluorescence assay (ELFA) and anti-HAV IgM were estimated using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Seroprotection rates were assessed using two cutoff levels for total anti-HAV antibodies (≥20 mIU/mL and ≥10 mIU/mL). Trends in geometric mean titers (GMTs) of anti-HAV antibodies over the last 20-years were evaluated. Of the 143 participants vaccinated in 2004, 99 could be followed up after 20 years. 12 were excluded and 87 participants (64.4% males), with mean (SD) age of 24.6 (2.6) years, were enrolled in the 20-year follow-up assessment. Seroprotection rates were 71.3% and 87.4% at anti-HAV cutoffs of ≥20 mIU/mL and ≥10 mIU/mL, respectively. None of the participants were positive for anti-HAV IgM and no breakthrough HAV infections were reported. A single dose of live attenuated HAV vaccine confers a durable protection and supports the potential utility of a single-dose strategy in endemic settings.

items.title: Hepatitis B Surface Antibody Seronegativity in Youth With ASD and Severe Behaviors: a Retrospective Tertiary Neurobehavioral Cohort.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B surface antibody (HBsAb) serostatus has received limited study in youth with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and severe behavioral needs. This study characterized HBsAb seronegativity in youth with ASD admitted to a tertiary neurobehavioral inpatient unit. We conducted a retrospective cohort review of patients applying for admission between 2016 and 2023. Eligible patients were ≤ 21 years of age with ASD and documentation of completion of the primary three-dose hepatitis B vaccine series. Pre-admission HBsAb results classified patients as responders or non-responders. Associations with age and sex were examined, and findings were compared descriptively with published benchmarks. Of 201 eligible patients, 81 (40.3%) were responders and 120 (59.7%) were non-responders (95% CI [52.6%, 66.5%]). Non-response prevalence was similar for males (59.0%) and females (62.2%). Older age was associated with lower odds of seroresponse, whereas sex was not significant after controlling for age. Because time since vaccination was unavailable, the age-related pattern may reflect waning detectable antibody rather than an ASD-specific difference in vaccine responsiveness. HBsAb seronegativity was common in this tertiary neurobehavioral cohort. However, the absence of a concurrently recruited, age- and time-since-vaccination-matched comparison group precludes attributing this finding to ASD. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether targeted post-series HBsAb testing may be useful in high-exposure clinical settings.

items.title: Risk of hepatitis B virus reactivation in adults with chronic hepatitis C receiving direct-acting antivirals: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection is a leading cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, affecting an estimated 50-57 million people worldwide. Although direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) have revolutionized HCV therapy, achieving >90-95% cure rates, hepatitis B virus (HBV)/HCV coinfection is still present in 1-15% of patients, raising HCC risk. This meta-analysis aims to estimate the pooled incidence of HBV reactivation in adults with chronic HCV infection treated with DAAs and to identify risk factors associated with reactivation. A comprehensive and systematic literature search was conducted across major databases including PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science, according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Eight randomized controlled trials and 19 observational cohort studies were included, which evaluated adult patients with chronic hepatitis C infection who were seropositive for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and received DAA therapy. The analysis of 27 studies encompassing 1707 HBsAg-positive patients revealed a substantial risk of virological HBV reactivation, with a pooled prevalence of 0.29 [95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.15-0.46; I2 = 97%]. Subgroup analysis showed a significantly lower reactivation rate in patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue prophylaxis (0.11 [95% CI = 0.05-0.22; I2 = 97%]) than those who did not (0.20 [95% CI = 0.09-0.36; I2 = 92%]). The pooled prevalence of clinical reactivation was 0.04 (95% CI = 0.02-0.07; I2 = 67%), which was also lower in the prophylaxis subgroup (0.03 vs. 0.07). The prevalence of alanine aminotransferase flare and HBV-associated hepatitis was 0.04 (95% CI = 0.02-0.06; I2 = 67%) for both, while the pooled prevalence of HBV DNA reappearance was 0.33 (95% CI = 0.18-0.50; I2 = 94%). HBV-related death was negligible (0.00, 95% CI = 0.00-0.01; I2 = 0%). Significant heterogeneity and publication bias were observed across most outcomes. HBV reactivation remains a clinically relevant problem in chronically HCV-infected patients treated with DAAs, particularly in HBsAg-positive patients or those not receiving HBV prophylaxis. Future research should focus on creating sophisticated risk prediction models of different prophylactic and monitoring strategies for preventing this burden of HBV reactivation with DAA use.

items.title: Per-protocol cure vs. intention-to-treat effectiveness of decentralised hepatitis C care in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review and single-arm proportional meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Reaching the World Health Organization (WHO) 2030 hepatitis C elimination targets in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) depends on decentralised, sub-national programmes, whose real-world cascade performance has not been quantitatively synthesised. We searched four bibliographic databases through May 2026, as well as regional and grey-literature sources, without language restrictions, to identify decentralised, subnational hepatitis C virus (HCV) programmes in LMICs that had implemented WHO-endorsed service delivery models from 2015 onwards. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted summary data, and assessed the risk of bias. Proportions were pooled using the Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine scale, with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp variance adjustment, and 95% prediction intervals were calculated. The co-primary outcomes were sustained virological response at 12 weeks (SVR12) among participants assessed for the outcome (per-protocol), SVR12 among all treatment initiators (intention-to-treat (ITT)), and treatment initiation (WHO indicator C7c). Prespecified subgroup, sensitivity, and certainty-of-evidence analyses were performed. Thirty-six reports describing 34 programmes in 18 countries were eligible, comprising 85,448 treatment initiators; none disaggregated outcomes by sex or gender, and most were at moderate risk of bias. Per-protocol SVR12 was 95.2% (95% confidence interval (CI) = 93.6-96.7; moderate certainty), whereas SVR12 across all initiators was 76.7% (95% CI = 68.9-83.6) and treatment initiation 87.8% (95% CI = 81.5-93.0), both of very low certainty. The within-programme gap had a median of 11.9 percentage points and exceeded 20 points in 12 programmes, reflecting attrition between treatment initiation and outcome ascertainment rather than virological failure. Heterogeneity was extreme and unexplained by units of decentralisation, delivery model, or income group. Decentralised HCV programmes in LMICs cure almost all patients who complete the cascade, but population-level effectiveness is substantially lower because of losses between treatment initiation and SVR12 ascertainment. Strengthening retention and outcome ascertainment, rather than drug efficacy, should be the priority for elimination; low-income countries remain markedly under-represented. PROSPERO: CRD420261384171.

items.title: Sustained Virological Response to Direct-Acting Antiviral Therapy for Hepatitis C Virus During Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: United States guidelines recommend consideration of direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment on an individual basis for pregnant women with hepatitis C virus (HCV), yet few data on safety and efficacy of DAAs in pregnancy are available. Our study aimed to pool sustained virological response (SVR) percentages from DAAs for HCV during pregnancy, to summarise adverse event data, and the infant's HCV and birth outcomes. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science on 09/11/2025 for post-01/01/2010 studies containing data on DAA treatment for HCV during pregnancy: the outcome of interest was the proportion with SVR (SVR%) after regimen completion. Data were extracted on adverse events, live births, and infant HCV status. A random-effects meta-analysis pooled the outcome percentages, with heterogeneity explored using the I 2 statistic. Of 523 studies screened, 13 were eligible (N = 228). The pooled SVR% of those tested was 100% (95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 100%-100%, I 2 : 0.0%). Of those finishing treatment the SVR% was 99% (95% CI: 90%-100%, I 2 : 31.2%). Excluding two studies of women pregnant whilst already on DAAs, the SVR% of those who started treatment was 91% (95% CI: 70%-100%, I 2 : 71.6%). Eight studies reported HCV testing of 75 infants, mostly from 6 months to 1 year after birth, with no active HCV (RNA) infections reported. One patient had vomiting as a treatment-related Grade 3 adverse event during pregnancy. High SVR percentages indicate DAAs' effectiveness at curing HCV during pregnancy, whilst maternal adverse events are rare. More data are needed on infant HCV status and safety outcomes.

items.title: Fully Synthetic Extracellular Vesicle-like Lipid Nanoparticles Recapitulate the Tumor Accumulation of Native Vesicles in NRAS-Mutant Melanoma.
items.abstract: NRAS-mutant melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer for which early detection and tumor targeting remain major clinical challenges. Although liposome-based nanotechnologies have been widely explored for cancer diagnosis and therapy, their tumor accumulation still largely relies on the enhanced permeability and retention effect, which is heterogeneous and often limits efficient penetration into solid tumors. In contrast, extracellular vesicles (EVs) exhibit efficient tumor penetration and intrinsic homing to their tumor of origin, but their clinical translation is hindered by challenges in scalable production and purification. To address these limitations, we engineered a fully synthetic EV-like nanoplatform that exhibits the tumor tropism of EVs derived from NRAS-mutant melanoma. EVs isolated from MUG Mel-2 NRAS-mutant melanoma cells and FOM-101 healthy melanocytes underwent comparative lipidomic and proteomic profiling to identify tumor-specific membrane signatures. Based on these data, we engineered synthetic liposomes that recapitulate the lipid composition of melanoma-derived EVs and incorporated selected tumor-associated proteins to reproduce EV biological function. The resulting EV-like nanoparticles showed favorable physicochemical properties, successful protein incorporation, and efficient internalization in NRAS-mutant melanoma cells. In vivo biodistribution studies in BALB/c nude mice bearing human melanoma xenografts demonstrated that EV-like nanoparticles reproduced the tumor accumulation of native EVs after intravenous administration. Nanoparticles mimicking the melanoma EV lipid composition accumulated in tumors even without protein enrichment, identifying lipids as active determinants of tumor homing, whereas physicochemically comparable conventional liposomes accumulated mainly in the liver. Protein incorporation, in particular CD98, further enhanced tumor accumulation and improved the tumor-to-liver distribution. Our findings demonstrate that this EV-inspired nanoplatform serves as a proof-of-concept tumor-homing system for NRAS-mutant melanoma, establishing a foundation for future therapeutic drug loading and targeted delivery applications.

items.title: Co-Delivery of Doxorubicin and Curcumin by a Graphene Oxide-β-Cyclodextrin-Based Drug Delivery System: In Vitro Anticancer Activity and In Vivo Pharmacokinetic, Biodistribution, and Toxicity Evaluation.
items.abstract: Liver cancer is the sixth most common cancer worldwide. Doxorubicin (DOX) as such induces cardiotoxicity, thereby restricting its clinical application in chemotherapy, so we have used curcumin (CUR) for diminishing the cardiotoxicity associated with DOX. In order to minimize the side effects of the anticancer drug, we have used glycyrrhetinic acid for targeting liver cancer cell lines. The prepared system is a polyelectrolyte of DOX and CUR-loaded aminated graphene oxide and β-cyclodextrin (AGO-GA-DOX-β-CD-CUR). Drug-loading efficiency (DLE) and encapsulation efficiency (DEE) for CUR in β-CD were found to be 27 ± 0.50% and 98 ± 1.20%, respectively. In AGO-GA-DOX-β-CD-CUR, the DLE and DEE for DOX were found to be 30 ± 0.20 and 99 ± 0.80%, respectively. DOX and CUR show a maximum release of 82 ± 4.04% and 65 ± 3.25%, respectively. The drug carrier shows an IC50 value of 70.24 μg/mL. The drug carrier shows potent anticancer activity and is confirmed by cell-cycle analysis. The formulation exhibited low hemolytic activity. Pharmacokinetic studies in healthy Wistar rats following oral administration revealed prolonged persistence of DOX and CUR compared with their respective free forms. In vivo fluorescence imaging further demonstrated the biodistribution of the formulation, while histopathological examination of the major organs revealed no remarkable tissue alterations following treatment with the dual-drug formulation. Overall, these findings highlight the potential of the AGO-GA-DOX-β-CD-CUR system as a dual-drug delivery platform, exhibiting promising in vitro anticancer activity along with favorable in vivo biodistribution and preliminary toxicity characteristics.

items.title: PIK3CA promotes hepatic tumor growth through evasion of phagocyte-mediated anti-tumor immunity.
items.abstract: Both primary and metastatic liver cancers are highly lethal diseases, for which effective treatment options remain limited. The unique hepatic microenvironment provides a niche that enables tumor cells to evade immune surveillance. To identify factors that mediate tumor growth within this immune microenvironment, we performed an in vivo RNAi screen to identify genes whose knockdown reduces liver tumor burden. We performed an in vivo RNAi screen by transplanting CT26 tumor cells into the liver of immunocompetent mice via hemi-spleen injection, aiming to compare gene essentiality in the liver versus in vitro cultured cells. The top hit depleted in vivo, Pik3ca, was validated in multiple syngeneic tumor models. Liver specificity of PIK3CA function was confirmed using an intracardiac injection model. To assess the contribution of T cells and phagocytes to tumor control, we employed TCR knockout mice and clodronate-mediated phagocyte depletion, respectively. Tumor progression and immune cell infiltration were analyzed via bioluminescence imaging and immunohistochemistry. Finally, the therapeutic efficacy of the PIK3CA inhibitor Alpelisib was evaluated in the hemi-spleen injection models of CT26 and Hepa1-6. Loss of Pik3ca in CT26 and Hepa1-6 cells markedly impaired tumor growth in the liver but not in subcutaneous sites or other organs, indicating a liver-specific dependency. Mechanistically, insulin and insulin-like growth factors-both enriched in the liver-activate their respective receptors to stimulate PIK3CA/AKT/mTOR signaling, thereby promoting tumor progression. Phagocyte depletion abrogated the anti-tumor effects of Pik3ca loss, whereas T cell deficiency had no impact, highlighting a phagocyte-mediated mechanism. Moreover, Pik3ca loss promoted F4/80 + macrophage infiltration into tumors. Treatment with the PIK3CA inhibitor Alpelisib recapitulated both the tumor suppression and the enhanced F4/80 + macrophage infiltration phenotypes observed in genetic models, confirming the therapeutic relevance of PIK3CA inhibition for treating hepatic malignancies. We identify PIK3CA as a key regulator of tumor-phagocyte interplay in the liver. Genetic or pharmacological targeting of PIK3CA suppresses liver tumor growth not through a direct, cancer cell-autonomous effect, but rather by activating phagocyte-mediated anti-tumor responses. These findings suggest that therapeutic strategies combining PI3K inhibition with immune modulation may be effective for treating liver malignancies driven by PI3K overactivation.

items.title: Histopathological observation and diagnosis of hepatic neuroendocrine carcinoma in a cat.
items.abstract: Hepatic neuroendocrine carcinoma is a rare hepatic neoplasm in cats. It is generally considered highly malignant with a poor prognosis. Therefore, early diagnosis and appropriate treatment of such tumors are critical for a successful outcome. This report describes a 6-year-old male Oriental Longhair cat presented to our hospital with a primary complaint of recurrent vomiting and mild abdominal distension. Ultrasonography revealed heterogeneous echogenicity of the hepatic parenchyma, indicating uneven hepatic density. Laparotomy revealed white and dark red nodules of varying sizes on the liver surface. Histopathological examination showed that the hepatic mass was composed of malignant neoplastic cells with typical neuroendocrine differentiation features. Immunohistochemical staining for CgA and NSE confirmed that the liver tumor cells were derived from the neuroendocrine system. Following histopathological diagnosis, the cat received palliative treatment and died 34 days after the initial presentation. Through histopathological observation and diagnosis of feline hepatic neuroendocrine carcinoma, this study provides a useful reference for the future clinical diagnosis of this disease.

items.title: Diagnostic and therapeutic challenges in brain metastases from differentiated thyroid carcinomas: insights from a tertiary, university-based center in Brazil.
items.abstract: We aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, treatment, and outcomes of patients with DTC who developed brain metastases (BM). We retrospectively analyzed patients with confirmed BM among 1532 patients with DTC followed at a university hospital in Brazil between 1986 and 2026. Data included demographic characteristics, treatments, clinical and radiological features, and outcomes. Overall survival from BM diagnosis was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Brain metastases occurred in 11 patients (0.7%), whose median ages at DTC and BM diagnosis were 54 and 57 years, respectively. Brain metastases were predominantly solitary (91%) and associated with peritumoral edema in 81.8% of patients. All patients had extracranial metastases, including the lungs (n = 8, 72.7%), bones (n = 8, 72.7%), liver (n = 2, 18.2%), adrenal glands (n = 1, 9.1%), and pleura (n = 1, 9.1%). Initial treatments included neurosurgery (n = 3), stereotactic radiosurgery (n = 5), and radioactive iodine (n = 2). One patient received exclusive palliative care. The median overall survival after BM diagnosis was 28 months, and seven patients (64%) died during follow-up. Patients with Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) <2 had better survival than those with ECOG ≥2 (72 vs. 8 months; p = 0.017). Brain metastases from DTC are associated with poor outcomes, and ECOG performance status at diagnosis may be an important prognostic factor for survival. Nonetheless, larger studies are needed to define optimal management strategies, particularly for patients with preserved performance status who may benefit from local treatment.
